items.title: 6.11.4 Calculating the entropy change of the system (reaction)

blocks.text: In order to calculate the entropy, change of the system we use the relationship:
Let us calculate the entropy change of the system for the reaction:

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned} S^\circ[\ce{Ca_{(s)}}] &= 41.40\ \text{J K}^{-1}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\\ S^\circ[\ce{O2_{(g)}}] &= 205.0\ \text{J K}^{-1}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\\ S^\circ[\ce{CaO_{(s)}}] &= 39.70\ \text{J K}^{-1}\,\text{mol}^{-1} \end{aligned}
blocks.text_alt: S°[Ca(s)] = 41.40 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; S°[O₂(g)] = 205.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; S°[CaO(s)] = 39.70 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned} \Delta S^\circ_{\text{system}} &= S^\circ_{\text{products}} - S^\circ_{\text{reactants}}\\ &= 2 \times S^\circ[\ce{CaO_{(s)}}] - \{2 \times S^\circ[\ce{Ca_{(s)}}] + S^\circ[\ce{O2_{(g)}}]\}\\ &= 2 \times 39.70 - \{(2 \times 41.40) + 205.0\}\\ &= 79.40 - 287.8\\ \Delta S^\circ_{\text{system}} &= -208.4\ \text{J K}^{-1}\,\text{mol}^{-1} \end{aligned}
blocks.text_alt: As ΔS°system = S°products – S°reactants = 2 × S°[CaO(s)] – {2 × S°[Ca(s)] + S°[O₂(g)]} = 2 × 39.70 – {(2 × 41.40) + 205.0} = 79.40 – 287.8; ΔS°system = –208.4 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹

blocks.text: The negative value for the entropy change shows that the entropy of the system has decreased. We know, however, that calcium reacts spontaneously with oxygen. So the entropy of the surroundings must also play a part because the total entropy change must be positive for the reaction to be feasible.
